description: Deadlines are absolute (lfdeadline, epoch ms) and checked by the consumer on every transport; the caller gets `expired`, never a silent wait.

cases.description: A call that finishes well inside its deadline replies normally.
A deadline already in the past when the consumer picks the call up: the node must not run (the consumer acknowledges and drops it); the caller sees `expired`.
The deadline passes while the node runs: the caller gets `expired` at the deadline, and the node's abort signal fires so it stops.
A reply that arrives after the deadline is ignored by the caller (no second outcome, no unhandled rejection); runners wait 1 s after the error and assert nothing else happened.
Every method carries a deadline, not only Execute.
